tr.name: Tricuspid regurgitation

mteer.title: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair · The Heart by Ultrasound

tteer.kicker: T-TEER, step by step: what TEE shows at each step
tteer.title: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair · The Heart by Ultrasound
tteer.description: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) joins the septal leaflet to the anterior or the posterior leaflet with a clip, brought from the femoral…

hcm.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy · The Heart by Ultrasound

lvad.name: Left ventricular assist devices
lvad.kicker: The HeartMate 3: the surveillance study, the speed ramp and complications
lvad.title: Left ventricular assist devices · The Heart by Ultrasound

pulse.q: A reflector lies at a depth of 8 cm. When does its echo arrive after the pulse is transmitted?
pulse.why: The round trip takes approximately 13 µs per centimeter of depth, so the echo arrives after 8 × 13 ≈ 104 µs.

pulse.q: The transmit frequency increases from 2.5 MHz to 5 MHz with 2 cycles per pulse. What happens to axial resolution?
pulse.why: The wavelength halves, so the spatial pulse length and the axial resolution halve. The depth of penetration decreases.

pulse.q: Why does the lung block the parasternal ultrasound beam?
opts: The tissue–air impedance difference causes almost total reflection
pulse.why: The acoustic impedance of air is far lower than that of soft tissue, so nearly all of the incident intensity is reflected at the tissue–air boundary.

image.q: An image is acquired at a depth of 16 cm with 100 scan lines and one focal zone. What is the approximate frame rate?
image.why: Each scan line takes 2 × 0.16 m ÷ 1540 m/s ≈ 208 µs. A frame of 100 lines therefore takes approximately 21 ms, which corresponds to approximately 48 frames per second.

image.q: Which change in the imaging settings increases the frame rate?
image.why: A narrower sector requires fewer scan lines for each frame, so each frame takes less time to acquire.

image.q: A second image of the heart appears behind the bright pleural line. Which artifact is this?
image.why: The pleura acts as an acoustic mirror and produces a copy of the structures in front of it at a position behind it.

windows.q: How is the parasternal short-axis view obtained from the parasternal long-axis view?
opts: Sliding the probe toward the apex
windows.why: In the ASE guideline, the probe is rotated 90° clockwise, so that the marker points to the left shoulder.

windows.q: In which position is the patient placed for parasternal and apical imaging?
windows.why: In the ASE guideline, parasternal and apical imaging is performed in the left lateral decubitus position, and subcostal and suprasternal imaging with the patient supine.

windows.q: How is the apical five-chamber view obtained from the apical four-chamber view?
opts: By moving the probe to the subcostal window
windows.why: In the ASE guideline, the five-chamber view is obtained by tilting the beam anteriorly from the four-chamber view.

planes.q: Which imaging planes intersect along the long axis of the LV?
opts: The apical four-, two- and three-chamber views
The parasternal long axis and the subcostal IVC view
planes.why: The apical planes are related by rotation about the LV long axis, so they intersect along it.

planes.q: Which apical view shows the LA, the mitral valve, the LVOT and the aortic valve?
planes.why: The ASE guideline lists the LA, MV, LV, LVOT, AV and aorta for the apical long-axis (three-chamber) view.

planes.q: The parasternal short-axis planes at the mitral valve and papillary muscle levels are…
planes.why: The probe is tilted between the levels, so the planes form a stack of nearly parallel sections.

cycle.q: Which valve event of the left heart coincides with the first heart sound?
cycle.why: Mitral valve closure coincides with the first heart sound (S1), and aortic valve closure coincides with the second heart sound (S2).

cycle.q: On Doppler recordings, the IVRT is measured from…
opts: the end of LVOT flow to the onset of the E wave
the onset of the E wave to the onset of the A wave
the QRS complex to aortic valve opening
cycle.why: The aortic and mitral valves are both closed from aortic valve closure, at the end of LVOT flow, to mitral valve opening, at the onset of the E wave.

cycle.q: Which frame defines end-diastole on echocardiography?
opts: The first frame after mitral valve closure
The peak of the T wave
cycle.why: In Lang 2015, end-diastole is defined as the first frame after mitral valve closure or the frame with the largest LV dimension.

loop.q: Afterload (Ea) increases while contractility (Ees) is unchanged. How does the EF change?
loop.why: Because EF = Ees ÷ (Ees + Ea), a larger Ea at the same Ees gives a lower EF.

loop.q: The slope of which relation is an index of contractility?
loop.why: The slope of the end-systolic pressure–volume relation, Ees, is a relatively load-independent index of contractility.

loop.q: In a ventricle with increased chamber stiffness, which change appears first on the pressure–volume loop?
opts: A steeper EDPVR, with a higher filling pressure at the same volume
A decrease in the ESPVR slope
A fall in Ea to zero
loop.why: Chamber stiffness is a passive property of the ventricle, so it changes the end-diastolic pressure–volume relation.

loop.q: Which phase of the pressure–volume loop is absent in chronic severe mitral regurgitation?
loop.why: The LV ejects into the LA from the onset of contraction, so LV volume decreases before the aortic valve opens.

shift.q: The angle between the Doppler beam and the flow is 60°. What fraction of the true velocity does the ultrasound system report?
shift.why: The reported velocity equals the true velocity × cos θ, and cos 60° = 0.5.

shift.q: A pulsed-wave Doppler signal aliases. Which change does NOT reduce the aliasing?
shift.why: A deeper sample volume lowers the PRF and therefore lowers the Nyquist limit.

shift.q: Why does continuous-wave Doppler not identify the depth at which the peak velocity originates?
opts: It samples every depth along the beam
It does not correct for the beam angle
shift.why: Continuous-wave Doppler transmits and receives continuously, so every depth along the beam contributes to the signal.

pressure.q: The LVOT area is 3.1 cm², the peak LVOT velocity is 1.0 m/s and the peak aortic velocity is 4.0 m/s. What is the aortic valve area?
pressure.why: The same flow passes both levels: 3.1 cm² × 1.0 m/s = AVA × 4.0 m/s, so the AVA is 3.1 ÷ 4 = 0.78 cm². The velocity ratio, 1.0 ÷ 4.0 = 0.25, also suggests severe stenosis.

pressure.q: Two patients have the same aortic valve and the same peak aortic velocity. In which one is the Doppler gradient most likely to exceed the catheter gradient from the LV to the aorta?
pressure.why: Past the valve, part of the pressure returns as the jet slows (pressure recovery). The recovery is larger in a small aorta and should be taken into account when the ascending aorta is narrower than 30 mm.

pressure.q: The peak TR velocity is 3.0 m/s. The IVC measures 2.4 cm at end-expiration and collapses by 30% with a sniff. What is the estimated RVSP?
pressure.why: The RV–RA pressure gradient is 4 × 3.0² = 36 mmHg. An IVC wider than 2.1 cm that collapses by less than 50% with a sniff gives an RA pressure of 15 mmHg, so the RVSP is 36 + 15 = 51 mmHg.

pressure.q: When must the velocity proximal to a stenosis be included in the Bernoulli equation?
pressure.why: The simplified equation neglects the proximal velocity; above 1.5 m/s, the proximal velocity is too large to be neglected.

eject.q: The apical views are foreshortened by 15%. What is the effect on the measured EDV and ESV?
eject.why: A plane that misses the true apex shortens the traced LV length, so both volumes are underestimated.

eject.q: An LVEF of 45% in a woman is classified as…
eject.why: According to Lang 2015, an LVEF of 41–53% is mildly abnormal in women.

eject.q: Global longitudinal strain is −15%. How is it classified?
eject.why: GLS is normal when more negative than −18%, borderline from −16% to −18%, and abnormal when less negative than −16%.

segments.q: The anterior wall, the anteroseptal wall and the apex are akinetic. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
segments.why: In the standard map, the LAD supplies the anterior and anteroseptal segments and the apex.

segments.q: Which apical view shows the inferior and anterior walls?
segments.why: In Lang 2015 (Figure 4), the two-chamber view shows segments 4, 10 and 15 of the inferior wall and segments 1, 7 and 13 of the anterior wall.

segments.q: Six of 16 segments are scored 3, and the other ten are normal. What is the wall motion score index?
segments.why: The index is the mean score, (6 × 3 + 10 × 1) ÷ 16 = 28 ÷ 16 = 1.75.

fill.q: A patient has a reduced e′, a normal E/e′, a normal peak TR velocity and an E/A of 0.7. What is the classification by the algorithm?
fill.why: Reduced e′ is the only abnormal first-step variable and E/A is ≤0.8, so the classification is grade 1 diastolic dysfunction with normal LA pressure.

fill.q: All three first-step variables are abnormal, and E/A is 2.5. What is the grade of diastolic dysfunction?
fill.why: Three abnormal first-step variables indicate a raised LA pressure, and a raised LA pressure with E/A ≥2 is classified as grade 3 diastolic dysfunction.

fill.q: In which of the following patients should this algorithm not be applied?
fill.why: The main algorithm applies to sinus rhythm; the guideline provides a separate approach for atrial fibrillation.

report.q: Where in the echocardiography report is the summary statement placed?
opts: At the top, after the demographics and indication
report.why: In the ASE 2025 reporting guideline, the summary statement is moved to the top of the report, after the demographic data and the indication.

report.q: Which term is recommended in place of “trivial” or “physiologic” for regurgitation that is less than mild?
report.why: The ASE 2025 guideline uses a single term, “trace”, for regurgitation that is less than mild.

report.q: How many LVEF values should be given in one echocardiography report?
report.why: The ASE 2025 guideline recommends that one LVEF value be reported, together with the method by which it was measured.

as.q: A patient has a peak aortic velocity of 3.6 m/s, a mean gradient of 30 mmHg, an AVA of 0.8 cm², a stroke volume index of 28 mL/m² and an LVEF of 60%. What is the most likely diagnosis?
as.why: A small valve area with a low gradient, low flow and a normal LVEF is consistent with paradoxical low-flow, low-gradient severe stenosis.

as.q: A patient has an LVEF of 35%, a peak aortic velocity of 3.4 m/s and an AVA of 0.8 cm². During low-dose dobutamine echocardiography, the area increases to 1.3 cm² and the velocity changes little. What is the most likely diagnosis?
as.why: An increase in area to above 1.0 cm² with increased flow suggests pseudo-severe stenosis; in true severe stenosis, the area remains ≤1.0 cm² and the velocity reaches 4 m/s.

as.q: In severe aortic stenosis without symptoms, which finding defines ACC/AHA stage C2?
as.why: Stage C2 is severe stenosis with LV systolic dysfunction, defined as an LVEF below 50%. A peak velocity of 5 m/s indicates very severe stenosis, which remains stage C1.

ms.q: The mitral pressure half-time is 200 ms. What is the mitral valve area by the pressure half-time method?
ms.why: By the pressure half-time method, the mitral valve area is 220 ÷ 200 = 1.1 cm².

ms.q: In mitral stenosis, the heart rate increases from 70 to 110 beats per minute. How does the mean transmitral gradient change?
ms.why: A faster heart rate shortens the diastolic filling period, so the transmitral flow rate and the mean gradient increase. The mean gradient should therefore be reported together with the heart rate.

ms.q: Which finding does the ACC/AHA guideline list as a consequence of severe mitral stenosis?
ms.why: The ACC/AHA guideline lists severe LA enlargement and a PA systolic pressure above 50 mmHg as consequences of severe mitral stenosis. The LV is usually normal in size.

mr.q: At a constant regurgitant flow, the aliasing velocity is lowered from 40 to 30 cm/s. How do the PISA radius and the EROA change?
opts: The radius increases; the EROA does not change
The radius increases; the EROA increases
mr.why: The flow, 2πr² × Va, is constant, so r² increases as Va decreases; the EROA, flow ÷ peak velocity, does not change.

mr.q: In mitral regurgitation, the EROA is 0.45 cm² and the regurgitant volume is 68 mL. What is the grade?
mr.why: An EROA ≥0.40 cm² and a regurgitant volume ≥60 mL meet the criteria for severe regurgitation.

mr.q: A patient with severe primary MR has no symptoms, an LVEF of 58% and an LV end-systolic diameter of 36 mm. What is the ACC/AHA stage?
mr.why: Stage C2 is defined by an LVEF ≤60% or an LV end-systolic diameter ≥40 mm. An LVEF of 58% alone is sufficient.

ar.q: The pressure half-time is 180 ms, holodiastolic flow reversal is present in the abdominal aorta, and the jet width is 70% of the LVOT diameter. What is the grade of aortic regurgitation?
ar.why: A pressure half-time below 200 ms, a jet width ≥65% of the LVOT diameter and holodiastolic flow reversal in the abdominal aorta all indicate severe AR.

ar.q: Why can the pressure half-time of the AR jet shorten without an increase in the severity of regurgitation?
ar.why: The pressure half-time depends on the diastolic pressure difference between the aorta and the LV. A higher LV diastolic pressure shortens it.

ar.q: A patient with chronic severe AR has no symptoms, an LVEF of 60% and an LV end-systolic diameter of 53 mm. What is the ACC/AHA stage?
ar.why: Stage C2 includes an LV end-systolic diameter above 50 mm (or above 25 mm/m²), even when the LVEF is normal.

peri.q: The end-diastolic echo-free space of a pericardial effusion measures 15 mm. How is the effusion graded?
peri.why: The ESC guideline grades an end-diastolic echo-free space of <10 mm as mild, of 10–20 mm as moderate and of >20 mm as large.

peri.q: Which echocardiographic finding is nearly 100% sensitive and specific for tamponade?
opts: RA collapse for more than one third of the cycle
peri.why: A brief RA inversion also occurs in the absence of tamponade, and a dilated IVC is sensitive but not specific. In the ASE guideline, RA collapse for more than one third of the cardiac cycle is the finding with this sensitivity and specificity.

peri.q: In the parasternal long-axis view, fluid lies between the descending aorta and the heart. Which fluid collection is it?
peri.why: According to the ASE guideline, pericardial fluid lies anterior to the descending aorta, whereas pleural fluid extends posterior to it.

peri.q: The septum shifts with respiration, the medial e′ is 12 cm/s and the hepatic vein expiratory diastolic reversal ratio is 0.65. Do the Mayo Clinic criteria indicate constrictive pericarditis?
opts: Yes: a septal shift with a medial e′ of 9 cm/s or more
No: the reversal ratio is below 0.79
No: all three findings are required
peri.why: The Mayo Clinic criteria require a respiratory septal shift together with a medial e′ of 9 cm/s or more or a reversal ratio of 0.79 or more. This combination had a sensitivity of 87% and a specificity of 91%. All three findings together raise the specificity to 97% but lower the sensitivity to 64%.

tr.q: Why is the regurgitant volume threshold for severe regurgitation lower for TR (45 mL) than for MR (60 mL) at the same EROA?
tr.why: The regurgitant volume equals EROA × VTI, and the lower TR velocity produces a smaller VTI.

tr.q: In torrential TR, the peak jet velocity is 1.8 m/s. What explains the low velocity?
opts: The RV and RA pressures approach each other
The Doppler beam is not aligned with the jet
tr.why: With a very large regurgitant orifice, the RA pressure rises toward the RV pressure, so the systolic pressure difference and the jet velocity decrease.

tr.q: Which hepatic vein flow pattern is specific for severe TR?
tr.why: Systolic flow reversal in the hepatic veins is specific for severe TR once other causes have been excluded.

rv.q: Which measure of RV systolic function is derived from the whole RV area in one plane?
rv.why: TAPSE and S′ measure the motion of a single point of the tricuspid annulus; FAC compares the RV areas at end-diastole and end-systole.

rv.q: In the short axis at the papillary muscles, the LV eccentricity index is 1.3 at end-diastole and 1.0 at end-systole. What does this pattern suggest?
rv.why: A septum flat at end-diastole only suggests RV volume overload. A septum flat at end-systole suggests RV pressure overload.

rv.q: The peak TR velocity is 3.1 m/s. The RVOT acceleration time is 90 ms and the RA area is 22 cm²; there are no other signs. What is the echocardiographic probability of PH (ESC/ERS 2022)?
rv.why: A velocity of 2.9–3.4 m/s gives an intermediate probability without other signs. Here the signs come from two categories, the pulmonary artery (acceleration time below 105 ms) and the RA (area above 18 cm²), so the probability is high.

rv.q: A patient with pulmonary hypertension has a TAPSE of 19 mm and an RV fractional area change of 30%. What explains the difference?
opts: The base of a failing, pressure-overloaded RV can keep its motion
TAPSE is measured at the wrong time
FAC is always lower than TAPSE
rv.why: TAPSE measures the longitudinal motion of the lateral annulus. In a maladapted RV the base often keeps its motion, so TAPSE can overestimate RV function; FAC also includes the radial motion of the free wall and the septum.

stress.q: A segment is normal at rest and becomes akinetic at peak dobutamine stress. What is the response?
stress.why: A new wall motion abnormality with stress in a segment that is normal at rest is an ischemic response.

stress.q: An akinetic segment improves at 10 µg/kg/min and is akinetic again at peak dose. What does this response indicate?
opts: Viable myocardium, ischemic at higher doses (biphasic response)
stress.why: Improvement at low dose shows contractile reserve, and worsening at higher doses shows ischemia. This biphasic response has the highest positive predictive value for recovery of function after revascularization.

stress.q: A 70-year-old patient reaches 120/min at peak dobutamine stress, with no wall motion abnormality. Is the stress adequate?
opts: Yes: any rise above the resting rate is enough
stress.why: The target is 85% of the age-predicted maximum, 0.85 × (220 − 70) ≈ 128/min. A test that does not reach the target heart rate is less sensitive for ischemia.

ivc.q: The IVC measures 2.4 cm at end-expiration and collapses by 30% with a sniff. What RA pressure is estimated?
ivc.why: An IVC wider than 2.1 cm that collapses by less than 50% with a sniff gives an RA pressure of 15 mmHg (range 10–20 mmHg) in the 2025 ASE guideline.

ivc.q: Where is the IVC diameter measured?
opts: At the diaphragm, from the apical window
1 to 2 cm from the RA junction, in the subcostal view
ivc.why: In the ASE guideline, the IVC is measured in the subcostal long-axis view, 1 to 2 cm from the right atrial junction, at its largest diameter, which usually occurs in expiration.

ivc.q: A patient receives positive-pressure ventilation. How is the IVC collapse used to estimate the RA pressure?
opts: As in a patient who breathes spontaneously
ivc.why: Under positive-pressure ventilation, the IVC collapse does not estimate the RA pressure. If the RA pressure is clinically relevant, an invasive measurement should replace the estimate.

ivc.q: In the subcostal view, which finding identifies the abdominal aorta rather than the IVC?
opts: It does not change with respiration
ivc.why: The aorta does not respond to respiration. Pulsation alone does not identify it: in hyperdynamic states and in TR, the IVC can pulse more than the aorta. The IVC, not the aorta, lies within the liver.

ai.q: In EchoPrime's anatomical attention, which view group carries the most weight for the IVC section?
ai.why: In the public weights, the IVC row is 1.00 for the subcostal group, 0.27 for the suprasternal group and 0.02 for the apical four-chamber group.

ai.q: How does EchoPrime give a number such as the LVEF?
opts: The mean of the values of the 50 most similar earlier studies
A caliper on the apical four-chamber frame with the largest LV
The LVEF of the single most similar study
ai.why: For each section, EchoPrime finds the 50 earlier studies whose embeddings lie closest. A number is their mean, and a finding is reported when more than half of them carry it.

ai.q: In a blinded randomized trial, a cardiologist finalized an initial LVEF from AI or from a sonographer. What was the result?
opts: The cardiologist changed the AI assessment less often (16.8% against 27.2%)
The cardiologist changed the AI assessment more often
ai.why: A change of more than 5% occurred in 16.8% of the AI assessments and 27.2% of the sonographer assessments; AI was non-inferior and superior.

ai.q: Which images were left out of EchoPrime's training?
ai.why: EchoPrime's encoder takes videos. Spectral Doppler and M-mode recordings are still images, so they were excluded from training.

measure.q: How does EchoNet-Measurements find the end of a caliper?
opts: The weighted center of a heat map that the model outputs
The brightest pixel of the image
An edge found by a fixed threshold
measure.why: Each model outputs a heat map for each point that it looks for, and the public code takes the weighted center of the map as the point.

measure.q: A video is exported without its DICOM header. What can the model still do?
opts: Find the caliper ends, but not convert them to centimeters
Nothing: it needs the header to find the points
measure.why: The points come from the image. The pixel size that converts pixels to centimeters, and the velocity per pixel of a Doppler image, come from the DICOM file.

measure.q: A heat map has two peaks of equal height, at the septum and at an RV trabeculation. Where does the point fall?
measure.why: The weighted center of two equal peaks lies midway between them, on neither structure, so the wall measures wrong.

shunts.q: Across a restrictive atrial communication, the peak septal velocity is 2.0 m/s, and the RA pressure is 8 mmHg. What is the peak LA pressure?
shunts.why: The peak LA–RA gradient is 4 × 2.0² = 16 mmHg. The peak LA pressure is the RA pressure + the gradient: 8 + 16 = 24 mmHg.

shunts.q: Why can the flow across a large secundum ASD not show a raised LA pressure?
opts: The flow is right to left
The atrial pressures equalize, so the gradient stays at about 1 mmHg
CW Doppler cannot record flow across the atrial septum
shunts.why: A large defect lets the LA and RA pressures equalize. In ASD the mean transatrial septal velocity is about 0.4 m/s, a gradient of about 1 mmHg, so the LA pressure is close to the RA pressure. Only a restrictive communication keeps a gradient that gives the LA pressure.

mteer.q: The sheath tents the fossa ovalis. In the four-chamber view, how high above the point where the clip will grasp should the tent be?
mteer.why: ASE 2026 gives about 4.5–5.0 cm above the point of grasp, which lies at or a little above the annulus for a flail or prolapse and can lie below it in secondary MR. The bicaval and short-axis views place the tent high and posterior.

mteer.q: Above the valve, the clip's arms are open and square to the line of coaptation. What does the commissural view (55–75°) show?
opts: The arms edge-on, as one line
The arms as a V, open toward the LV
mteer.why: The commissural view lies along the line of coaptation, so the two arms, square to it, show edge-on, as one line. The long-axis view (100–160°) shows both arms at full length.

mteer.q: Two thin jets remain after the clip, one on each side of it. How is the residual MR graded?
opts: By PISA and the EROA of each jet
By the vena contracta of each jet and the other signs, not by PISA
By the sum of the color jet areas
mteer.why: The clip distorts the hemispheric flow convergence that PISA assumes, and there are often two or more jets, so ASE 2019 and 2026 do not recommend PISA after TEER. A vena contracta of 0.7 cm or more in any jet is specific for severe MR; with several jets, 3D TEE adds their vena contracta areas.

mteer.q: Before release, the mean gradient across the double orifice is measured. Which result does ASE 2026 prefer?
opts: Under 5 mmHg, with a valve area of 2.0 cm² or more
Under 10 mmHg at any heart rate
Any value, if the MR is mild
mteer.why: ASE 2026 prefers a residual mean gradient under 5 mmHg with a valve area of 2.0 cm² or more, reported with the heart rate. In 268 patients, an invasive gradient above 5 mmHg just after implantation predicted a worse long-term outcome.

tteer.q: Which pair of leaflets can a tricuspid clip grasp to reduce TR?
opts: The septal leaflet with the anterior or the posterior leaflet
Any two leaflets, with the same effect
tteer.why: The septal leaflet is grasped with the anterior or the posterior leaflet. A grasp of the anterior and posterior leaflets alone has not been shown to reduce TR. Without a focal defect, the anteroseptal line, usually the longest, comes first.

tteer.q: The arms lie square to the anteroseptal line of coaptation. Which view shows their orientation most accurately?
opts: The 3D en face view of the valve
The parasternal long axis on TTE
tteer.why: The 3D en face view, with multiplanar reconstruction to place the two 2D planes at the site of the grasp, shows the orientation most accurately. The transgastric short axis of the leaflet tips is the other check, with care for off-axis cuts.

tteer.q: After the grasp, the residual TR must be graded. Which method grades it best with a clip in place?
opts: The color jet area in the RA
tteer.why: With a clip in place, PISA tends to overestimate the residual TR. The 3D vena contracta area grades it best.

tteer.q: In TRILUMINATE Pivotal, which outcome carried the primary end point at 1 year?
tteer.why: Death or tricuspid surgery and heart failure hospitalization did not appear to differ at 1 year. The KCCQ score rose by 12.3 points with TEER and by 0.6 points with medical therapy alone. In the hierarchy, a KCCQ gain of at least 15 points gave 21% of the wins to TEER and 7% to the control group.

tavr.q: Where is the aortic annulus measured on TEE to size a transcatheter valve?
opts: At the sinotubular junction, in diastole
At the hinge points of the cusps, in systole, inner edge to inner edge
At the tips of the open cusps, in systole
tavr.why: The annulus that sizes the valve is the diameter at the hinge points of the cusps, measured in systole on a zoomed long axis, inner edge to inner edge (ASE 2022). CT is the reference for sizing; 3D TEE measures 3.5–7.4% smaller, usually without a change of valve size (EACVI 2023).

tavr.q: A 26-mm SAPIEN 3 sits across the annulus before its balloon is inflated. What final depth is the target?
opts: 80/20 to 90/10 of the frame's height, aortic to ventricular
50/50: the middle of the frame at the annulus
The whole frame below the annulus, in the LVOT
tavr.why: A SAPIEN 3 is placed for a final depth of 80/20 to 90/10 of its frame's height, aortic to ventricular (Blackman 2021). The frame shortens as it expands, mostly at its ventricular end, from 27 to 20 mm for the 26-mm valve (Schymik 2015), so that end rises toward the annulus as the balloon fills.

tavr.q: At the check, two paravalvular jets take 20% of the frame's circumference. What is the grade?
tavr.why: The circumferential extent is the sum of the jets' vena contracta arcs divided by the circumference of the valve's outer edge: less than 10% is mild, 10–29% moderate and 30% or more severe, best read with the vena contracta (ASE 2024). A jet counts only where it enters the LV at the frame's ventricular edge; color in the sinuses above the skirt is not a leak (ASE 2019).

tavr.q: Which result meets the valve's intended performance in VARC-3?
opts: A mean gradient of 25 mmHg and a DVI of 0.40
A mean gradient of 10 mmHg, a peak velocity of 2.2 m/s, a DVI of 0.46 and mild paravalvular regurgitation
A peak velocity of 3.4 m/s with no regurgitation
tavr.why: VARC-3 asks for a mean gradient below 20 mmHg, a peak velocity below 3 m/s, a DVI of 0.25 or more and less than moderate regurgitation (Généreux 2021). Mild paravalvular regurgitation meets it; with the SAPIEN 3, at least moderate regurgitation at 30 days carried a hazard ratio of 2.40 for death at 1 year (Pibarot 2017).
